text:
Alex: heads-up, I ran a quick perf sweep on rti-kernel-selector w/ continuous batching enabled. seeing a weird knee at seq_len=128 where launch overhead + kernel switch kills throughput.

Maria: ugh that matches the flaky regression we saw yesterday on canary. numbers? :eyes:

Alex: baseline (no kernel switch): 22.1k toks/s at seq=64, 18.3k toks/s at seq=128. with autotuner on (path switch allowed): 17.6k toks/s at 128 and 12.9k toks/s at 256. launch latency per request spikes ~1.7ms on switches.

Jordan: can you paste the perf log and the selector decision trace? want to see why it switches at 128.

Alex: pasted below (trimmed):
```
[2024-11-02T10:12:34Z] request id=abc123 seq_len=128 decided_rule=seqlen_threshold kernel=v1.2.0 path=hybrid-switch
[...]
profile: kernel_v1.2.0 latency=0.9ms tail_latency=1.3ms throughput=17.8k
profile: kernel_v1.3.1 latency=0.6ms tail_latency=0.8ms throughput=19.6k
launch_overhead: cold_switch=1.7ms hot_switch=0.5ms
batching: cont_batch enabled avg_shape=[1,64,1] adjust_delay=0.65ms
```

Sam: interesting — autotuner picked v1.2.0 for 128 because of expected single-token latency shaping (profiled earlier on A100 gen1). but our continuous batching shape distribution now has a much higher fraction of multi-token requests so the earlier kernel perf prediction is stale.

Maria: so the scheduler is using stale per-arch profiles. how often do we refresh kernel profiles on dedicated fleets?

Sam: currently daily for prod fleets, but our nightly job doesn't sample long-tail seq distributions. we only benchmark typical prompt shapes (<=64) so seq=128 skew is unseen.

Jordan: two quick mitigations: 1) add a lightweight on-path microbenchmark that runs when kernel switch is considered, sampling the current batch-shape for a few iterations (cheap). 2) bias the autotuner cost model to include launch_overhead * probability_of_switch (estimated from request mix).

Alex: implemented a POC microbenchmark: it runs 10 warmup inferences with the current batch shape and measures cold_switch vs hot_switch. adds ~0.2ms to decision path when triggered. results: decision now prefers v1.3.1 for 128 -> throughput back to 19.2k.

Maria: nice. any KV-cache interactions? earlier we saw switch causing KV invalidation and extra copy cost.

Alex: yes — when switching kernels we were recreating kv-buffers on the heap which caused a 0.6ms penalty. fixed by reusing a pooled kv-buffer and adding a small compatibility shim so kv-layout matches both kernels. after that, cold_switch dropped from 1.7ms -> 1.05ms.

Sam: can we avoid switches mid-batch entirely? maybe only allow switches between batches if predicted speedup > threshold t. also consider sticky-path for a session to prevent oscillation.

Jordan: agree. set threshold = launch_overhead + kv_rebind_cost + 0.2ms margin. and implement sticky session TTL=2s. reduces churn on bursty clients.

Maria: let's also add logging for decision entropy per-minute so we can alert if the selector flips >10x/min. that was the symptom in the regression incident.

Alex: will PR: rti-select: add microbench, add kv reuse shim, add sticky-session support, log entropy. bench harness improvements included.

ci-bot: CI pipeline started for branch alex/kernel-selector-microbench — tests: unit, integration, perf-smoke. :rocket:

Sam: will run a canary in cluster dev-fleet-3 for 2 hours with cont-batching enabled and new selector. I'll collect perf/trace and post numbers.

Alex: thanks — posting initial canary after 30m. so far 19.1k @128 stable, tail latency p95 down 18%. :thumbsup:

Maria: awesome. follow-up: add nightly reprofile job that includes seq_len stratified sampling (up to 512) so autotuner learns current mix. create a ticket?

Jordan: created ticket INF-7282. assign to infra-bench team.

Alex: I'll link PR to INF-7282.

Sam: p.s. we should add a small note in the runbook about kernel-switch fallout (kv rebind + launch cost) so oncall knows the typical mitigation steps.

Maria: agreed. I'll update runbook after canary completes. :memo:
